To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
model-based reinforcement learning with self-play can achieve the optimal sample complexity in multi-agent reinforcement learning.

model-based algorithms are provably sample-efficient in multi-agent reinforcement learning, and the sample complexity of model-based algorithms is optimal up to a $\min\{\text{\#actions for each player}\}$ factor.

model-based reinforcement learning with self-play is able to output single Markov policies that are provably as sample efficient as the information-theoretically lower bound, and that our algorithmic design and analysis techniques are broadly applicable for multi-player general sum Markov games.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (a) can model-based algorithms achieve the optimal sample complexity in multi-agent Markov game? (b) can model-based self-play achieve the same sample complexity as model-free self-play?
the following question: \emph{Can model-based algorithms for multi-agent reinforcement be as sample-efficient as their single-agent counterparts?
understanding the sample efficiency of model-based algorithms, and provides a sharp analysis that is the best known for multi-agent reinforcement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our paper is the first to present provably efficient model-based algorithms for multi-agent reinforcement leaning in Markov games.
our analysis provides the first sharp sample complexity guarantee for multi-agent reinforcement algorithms, and the first that matches information-theoretic bounds in the model-based setting.

our work closes the gap between the model-based and model-free algorithms in terms of sample complexity for multi-agent reinforcement leaning in zero-sum Markov Games, and provides the first line of efficient algorithms in the multi-player general-sum setting.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

for the first time we are able to provide a sharp analysis for model-based algorithms in multi-agent reinforcement learning, and the sample complexity we achieve is comparable with model-free algorithms.
we provide the first provably efficient model-based algorithm for multi-agent reinforcement, and the first that achieves sample efficiency matching the information-theoretically lower bound.
we provide the first provably efficient model-based self-play algorithm for multi-agent Markow games, which is able to output a single Nash policy and achieves the best known sample complexity.
The main takeaway from our work is that

for multi-agent reinforcement leaning with self-play, model-based algorithms are still sample-efficient even though their sample efficiency is worse than that of model-free algorithms in the single-agent setting.
, model-based algorithms are also able to achieve the best sample complexity for multi-agent Mark ov games.
model-based algorithms for multi-agent reinforcement are not only practical, but also sample-efficient.
